Six Degrees of South Carolina

A living map of who knows whom across the Palmetto State — every circle a person, every gold thread a friendship.

Click A Person
Highlights them and zooms in close. Step outward from 0° (just them) to 6° — friends of friends of friends… Prefer seeing the whole ring at once? Switch "On Select" to Big Picture in settings.
Click A County
Turns it gold and lists everyone who lives there.
Search
Find anyone by name, town, or county.
Filters
Gate the map by friend count, tie strength, mutual friends, reach, county, interests, and political issues. Hover any control for a hint.
Lines
Shows or hides the connecting lines for whoever you have picked. With nobody picked there is nothing to draw, so the map stays clean until you choose someone. Hovering anyone previews their own ties either way.
Line Styles
A line's degree is how many pieces it is broken into: 1° runs unbroken, 2° breaks in two, 3° in three, out to 6°. Count the pieces to read the degree. Fine dots mean a mutual tie between two people on the same ring, which is not a step outward. Short lines stay solid — there isn't room to count them.
What's A Ring?
Everyone at exactly one degree from your selection. Ring 1 is their friends, ring 2 is friends of friends, and so on. The ring you're currently on is drawn brightest and thickest; the rings inside it recede.
Find A Path
Open anyone's profile and hit Find A Path, then pick a second person — the shortest chain of friendships between them lights up, hop by hop.
Compare Two People
Compare With on a profile shows their mutual friends, shared interests, shared issues, and how many hops apart they are.
Challenge
The target button in the menu bar drops you on a stranger and dares you to reach another one, hopping friend to friend. Beat the shortest route if you can.
Move Around
Drag to pan · scroll or pinch to zoom · double-click to zoom in.
Keyboard
Tab to the map, then arrow keys pan, +/− zoom, 0 resets, Esc clears the selection.

Node size tracks friend count; line weight and brightness track how often two people interact. Placement clusters households and friend groups near their real towns, inside their real county.

PROOF OF CONCEPT. Every name, profile, and friendship shown here is fabricated for demonstration. Photos are used with the map owner's permission.

HOW THE NETWORK IS BUILT. The friendships are invented, but the shape of the network is calibrated against measured research: household sizes from the Census ACS for South Carolina, a distance-decay exponent of −2.0 fitted to Meta's county-level Social Connectedness Index, and per-county clustering from Chetty et al.'s Social Capital Atlas, which finds rural counties measurably more clustered than urban ones. Tie strength tracks how embedded a friendship is rather than how short it is — strong ties sit inside dense clusters, weak ties bridge between them.

ONE CAVEAT WORTH KNOWING. About 41% of a real South Carolinian's friendships are with people living outside the state. This map holds only South Carolinians, so it models the within-state slice of the network, and every target it is calibrated against has been renormalised to that slice. Read the degrees as "degrees of separation within South Carolina," not across the whole of someone's life.
